- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect potential rebound.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30d forecasts when sentiment is low or neutral — adjust upward by 2–5% for such cases.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts continued rise — cap forecast growth to 3–5% per day to avoid lagged overcorrection.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 85), model tends to ignore it — reduce forecast slope and add 1–2% downward bias.
- When sentiment history shows increasing positivity (e.g., 3+ consecutive >0.2), model may overfit recent trend — apply smoothing or reduce forecast momentum by 10–15%.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14d average, adjust forecast to align with 14d moving average unless sentiment strongly contradicts it.
